A_target.statement:
Assume the [[Axiom of Countable Choice]].
Then a [[Definition:Countable Union|countable union]] of [[Definition:Countable Set|countable sets]] is countable.

B_source.statement:
The [[Definition:Cantor Pairing Function|Cantor pairing function]]:
:$\map \pi {m, n} = \dfrac {\paren {m + n} \paren {m + n + 1} } 2 + n$
is a [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] $\N \times \N \to \N$.

substitutions.pairs (m, n): pairs (index of a set, index within that set)

derived.a surjection from N x N: a surjection from N onto the union

object_map.reformulation: Enumerate each set, combine the enumerations into one map on N x N, and compose with the pairing bijection.

validity_conditions: Countable choice is needed to choose an enumeration of each set simultaneously.
Without choice, the real numbers can be a countable union of countable sets.
proof_plan:
Let $A_0, A_1, \ldots$ be countable, and discard the empty ones.
By countable choice, choose surjections $f_i: \N \to A_i$.
Then $\map F {i, n} = \map {f_i} n$ defines a surjection $F: \N \times \N \to \bigcup_i A_i$.
By the source result, $F \circ \pi^{-1}: \N \to \bigcup_i A_i$ is a surjection.

Sending each element to its least preimage gives an injection into $\N$, so $\bigcup_i A_i$ is countable.
{{qed}}
